comparisons.reason: The two features measure different constructs. Feature 0 is 1 if any comment engages in any way (addresses, questions, rebuts, accepts or builds on) a specific example or premise the OP cited. Engagement need not be critical, and the target is any cited example or premise. Feature 26 is 1 only if a comment states in its own voice that the OP's central initial premise is valid, and does so before it introduces its disagreement. That requires an explicit validity acknowledgment, a specific target (the central premise), and a within-comment ordering. A comment that rebuts a cited example would count for 0 but not for 26. The null rules also differ: 0 returns null when OP context is insufficient to determine the target, while 26 returns null only when title and argument are both missing.
